title: Spatial clusters reduced threshold detection in 33 PTWC threat pairs from 2014 to 2026
abstract: We test how the joint selection of tide-gauge sites changes detection of first PTWC threat thresholds. We reuse a fixed archive and retain 33 event-region pairs in 15 earthquakes with at least six distinct sites. Each site has the same inclusion probability under three designs. Reading half the sites in geographic clusters gives mean detection of 53.88%, compared with 56.82% for uniform random subsets. The paired difference is -2.94 percentage points (earthquake-bootstrap 95% interval -5.59 to -0.51). Spread selection gives 57.67%, with no clear gain over random selection. The cluster effect remains negative when any one earthquake is omitted. We prove sharp detection bounds over all fixed-size, equal-inclusion designs and verify them by finite linear programs. Their mean interval is 34.66-60.40% for half the sites. The bounds concern recorded sites and do not identify a true coastal maximum. This is a method study on an earlier archive, not an independent forecast validation or a test of actual sensor failures.

display.caption: Detection probabilities under equal-inclusion site selection. Bars are means across 33 pairs. Error bars are earthquake-bootstrap 95% intervals. Shading gives mean sharp bounds over all fixed-size equal-inclusion designs; it is not a confidence interval.
